evals.prompt: I need a CONSORT participant flow diagram for my RCT going to a journal: 500 assessed for eligibility, 150 excluded, 350 randomized into a treatment arm (n=175) and control arm (n=175), with lost-to-follow-up and final analyzed counts.
evals.expected_output: Invokes alterlab-scientific-schematics on its keyless path: draws the CONSORT 2010 flowchart as code (SVG, e.g. from assets/consort_template.svg, or TikZ) with every count copied from trial_flow_counts.md, renders it locally (generate_schematic.py / figure_tools.py, cairosvg) to a versioned PNG in figures/ plus a vector PDF/SVG, then reviews the render itself on scientific accuracy, clarity, labels, layout, and professional appearance against the journal document-type threshold (8.5/10), revising at most twice and recording scores in a JSON review log. No API key is asked for.

assertions.value: Builds the diagram as rendered code (SVG or TikZ to PNG/PDF) and applies the journal-tier quality threshold (8.5/10) in a review of the rendered image, not an ASCII or text-only diagram.
Uses the counts in the attached trial_flow_counts.md instead of asking for them or inventing them: exclusions 98 / 41 / 11, lost to follow-up 9 (treatment) and 12 (control), analysed 166 and 163.

evals.prompt: Create a transformer encoder-decoder architecture diagram for my conference paper, showing the encoder stack on the left, decoder stack on the right, multi-head self-attention, masked attention, and the cross-attention connection between them.
evals.expected_output: Invokes alterlab-scientific-schematics on its keyless path: draws the transformer architecture as SVG or TikZ with the requested layout (encoder stack left, decoder stack right, N x frames, multi-head self-attention, masked self-attention in the decoder, and the encoder-to-decoder cross-attention connection), renders it locally, and reviews the render against the conference threshold (8.0/10) with up to 2 iterations. Output is a versioned PNG, a vector copy, the source, and a review log; no API key is needed.

evals.prompt: Draw the MAPK signaling pathway from the EGFR receptor through RAS, RAF, MEK, ERK to nuclear gene transcription, with each arrow labeled as phosphorylation or activation, for an academic poster.
evals.expected_output: Invokes alterlab-scientific-schematics on its keyless path: draws the EGFR -> RAS -> RAF -> MEK -> ERK -> nuclear transcription cascade as SVG or TikZ with every arrow labelled as phosphorylation or activation, renders it locally at poster size, and reviews the render against the poster threshold (7.0/10), stopping once met; output is a versioned PNG plus vector copy and review log.

evals.prompt: I want a block diagram of an IoT system: sensors feeding a microcontroller, then a WiFi module to a cloud server and a mobile app, with the connections labeled by protocol (I2C, UART, WiFi, HTTPS).
evals.expected_output: Invokes alterlab-scientific-schematics on its keyless path: draws a layered block diagram as SVG (sensors -> microcontroller -> WiFi module -> cloud server -> mobile app) with each connection labelled by its protocol (I2C, UART, WiFi, HTTPS), renders it locally, and reviews the render against the document-type threshold with up to 2 iterations. Output is a versioned PNG, vector copy, and review log.

evals.prompt: I have an OpenRouter key set up. Generate the MAPK pathway figure for my poster with the Nano Banana image model rather than drawing it by hand: EGFR to RAS, RAF, MEK, ERK, then nuclear gene transcription.
evals.expected_output: Invokes alterlab-scientific-schematics on its optional AI backend because the user asked for the image model by name: runs scripts/generate_schematic.py with the cascade description, -o to a figures/ PNG, --doc-type poster and --backend ai (Nano Banana 2 generation, Gemini 3.1 Pro Preview review against the 7.0/10 poster threshold, max 2 iterations, review log written). Warns that the prompt goes to OpenRouter and that the model draws the labels itself, so each protein name and arrow must be checked on the result.

assertions.value: Uses the AI backend explicitly (--backend ai) with the poster document type, and tells the user to check the generated labels against the pathway.

evals.prompt: Add a flowchart of our experiment decision logic to the README as version-controllable text that renders on GitHub and diffs cleanly in git.
evals.expected_output: Does NOT invoke this skill; defers to alterlab-mermaid. The user explicitly wants a text-based, git-diffable diagram that renders on GitHub, not a rendered PNG — the skill's own description routes text-based Mermaid diagrams to alterlab-mermaid.

evals.prompt: Make me a photorealistic cover illustration of a futuristic neuroscience lab with glowing brain scans for my talk's title slide.
evals.expected_output: Does NOT invoke this skill; defers to alterlab-generate-image. This is a general photo/illustration/artwork request, not a technical or scientific diagram of concepts and relationships — the skill's description routes general photos, illustrations, or artwork to alterlab-generate-image.

evals.prompt: Turn our trial's headline results — enrollment, response rate, and top three findings — into an eye-catching infographic for the department newsletter.
evals.expected_output: Does NOT invoke this skill; defers to alterlab-infographics. A general-audience graphic that presents headline statistics is an infographic (type presets, styles, research-backed numbers), not a technical or methodology schematic.
